application_review: Under the actual unnormalized weighted law, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz derives every fixed product moment from single-factor moments and derives a vanishing L1 product from a vanishing L2 factor and a bounded L2 factor.
A finite telescoping product proves vanishing weighted mixed-product clipping error, including the empty product, without assuming any product moment or independence.
The actual original weighted harmonic root mass tends to two and is eventually at most three; original normalized single-dual moments give each factor a bounded weighted moment class.

Original normalized mixed local dual products with different dimensions, prime arities, denominators and valid gaps retain vanishing weighted clipping error under one fixed master and explicit polynomial inclusion conditions.
Using |nu-1|<=1+nu, the actual derived mixed clipping estimate transfers the original centered root product limit to its clipped product, including zero replicas.
The clipping threshold is monotone in dimension. One fixed threshold above A_d applies to any stage-wise choice from a fixed finite family of original profiles.

Arbitrary admissible sequence convergence implies qualitative uniform vanishing by selecting a bad input whenever one exists. This is instantiated for original clipped dual products, uniformly over finite profiles and all simultaneously admissible input families under fixed master/template/gap/J data. No quantitative rate or dense-model conclusion is claimed.

All weighted root-mass, single-factor moment and clipping inputs in the mixed application are derived from previously proved actual-law theorems; no desired product bound or clipping limit is supplied.
The original separately conditioned local prime laws, their own designated denominators, shifts, quotient lengths and coefficients remain unchanged.

The fixed original master family, arity and polynomial list do not depend on replica count or profile. Concrete original correlation polynomial template construction and fixed-list membership are still explicit inputs.

The uniform conclusion ranges over all simultaneously admissible profile input families with the fixed admissible template/gap/J data. Extending arbitrary single-profile inputs by zeros has not been separately formalized; no uniform quantitative rate is asserted.
Uniformity follows by applying the actual finite-profile clipped limit to every chosen sequence of epsilon and vertex tests; it is not a generic supplied-limit bridge presented as a concrete proof.
Signed convex combinations, polynomial approximation, closed convex hulls, separation/minimax, dense models, Prediction/Alignment and the final StrongConjecture proof remain unfinished.
StrongStatement.lean is unchanged; StrongConjecture remains a named proposition, and strong_implies_subtype requires it as a hypothesis.

All 301 baseline hashes were revalidated unchanged before registration. Only root imports and the exact-name registry changed among retained hashed files. Runtime, dependency and attributed PNT+ files remain unchanged.
